questions.stem: This high-power H&E field from an enlarged lymph node shows a large malignant cell (bracketed) with a bilobed 'owl-eye' nucleus and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli. This cell is diagnostic of which condition?

explanation.summary: The bilobed, owl-eye Reed-Sternberg cell with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli is the pathognomonic histologic finding of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, roughly half of which are EBV-associated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bilobed, owl-eye Reed-Sternberg cell with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli is the pathognomonic histologic finding of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, roughly half of which are EBV-associated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia shows sheets of small mature lymphocytes and smudge cells, not large binucleate cells with huge nucleoli.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Burkitt lymphoma shows monotonous medium-sized cells with a starry-sky pattern, not scattered Reed-Sternberg cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Follicular lymphoma shows crowded neoplastic follicles of centrocytes and centroblasts without owl-eye cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is EBV-associated but shows nests of undifferentiated epithelial cells, not bilobed lymphoid owl-eye cells.

questions.stem: This histology field of a highly mitotic B-cell neoplasm shows dense sheets of neoplastic cells interspersed with scattered pale tingible body macrophages. What is this classic low-power pattern called?

explanation.summary: The pale tingible body macrophages scattered among the dark neoplastic B-cells create the 'starry sky' appearance characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pale tingible body macrophages scattered among the dark neoplastic B-cells create the 'starry sky' appearance characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The owl-eye pattern describes the paired nuclei of Reed-Sternberg cells in Hodgkin lymphoma, or CMV inclusions, not a low-power field.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Signet-ring cells have intracellular mucin pushing the nucleus aside, as in diffuse gastric carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Onion-skin lamellation describes concentric layers, as in hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis or Ewing sarcoma periosteal reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A storiform pattern is a cartwheel arrangement of spindle cells, as in dermatofibrosarcoma or IgG4-related fibrosis.

questions.stem: This histologic field from an EBV-positive nasopharyngeal tumor shows nests of undifferentiated epithelial cells admixed with abundant background lymphocytes. Which histologic subtype does this represent?

explanation.summary: The EBV-associated non-keratinizing (undifferentiated) subtype of nasopharyngeal carcinoma shows undifferentiated epithelial cells with a dense lymphocytic infiltrate.
explanation.whyCorrect: The EBV-associated non-keratinizing (undifferentiated) subtype of nasopharyngeal carcinoma shows undifferentiated epithelial cells with a dense lymphocytic infiltrate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Verrucous carcinoma is a well-differentiated exophytic squamous tumor with pushing borders, unrelated to EBV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Keratinizing squamous carcinoma shows keratin pearls and intercellular bridges and is the subtype least associated with EBV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Basaloid squamous carcinoma forms nests of small basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and comedonecrosis, not EBV-driven undifferentiated cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adenocarcinoma forms glands and is not the EBV-associated lymphocyte-rich nasopharyngeal pattern.

questions.stem: This electron micrograph of a malignant lymphocyte shows a strikingly multi-lobulated, flower-shaped nucleus. This 'flower cell' is characteristic of the acute phase of which malignancy?

explanation.summary: A multi-lobulated, flower-shaped nucleus is seen in the acute phase of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma associated with HTLV-1 infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: A multi-lobulated, flower-shaped nucleus is seen in the acute phase of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma associated with HTLV-1 infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic myeloid leukemia shows maturing granulocytes with basophilia; it lacks lymphocytes with flower-shaped nuclei.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hairy cell leukemia cells have fine hair-like cytoplasmic projections and oval nuclei, not multilobed nuclei.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Burkitt lymphoma cells are medium-sized with round nuclei and vacuolated basophilic cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hodgkin lymphoma is identified by Reed-Sternberg cells with owl-eye nucleoli, not flower cells.

questions.stem: These gastric mucosa panels show normal antrum (left) versus mucosa colonized by H. pylori (right) that has developed a dense inflammatory infiltrate. Which inflammatory cells predominate in this chronic response?

explanation.summary: H. pylori induces chronic gastritis characterized by a mucosal infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells, the first step in the cascade toward adenocarcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: H. pylori induces chronic gastritis characterized by a mucosal infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells, the first step in the cascade toward adenocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neutrophils mark active H. pylori gastritis, but the dense chronic infiltrate is mainly lymphocytes and plasma cells; eosinophils are minor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mast cells and basophils mediate allergic reactions and do not dominate H. pylori gastritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multinucleated giant cells belong to granulomas, as in Crohn disease, which H. pylori does not typically produce.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Foamy macrophages accumulate in xanthomas or certain infections like Whipple disease, not as the main H. pylori infiltrate.

questions.stem: The right panel shows gastric mucosa that has acquired goblet cells and Paneth cells with red granules (arrows) in response to chronic H. pylori injury, compared with atrophic gastritis on the left. What is the significance of this change?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a normal variant of antral mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a premalignant metaplastic change

explanation.summary: Intestinal metaplasia (goblet and Paneth cells replacing gastric epithelium) is a premalignant step in the H. pylori-driven progression toward gastric adenocarcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intestinal metaplasia (goblet and Paneth cells replacing gastric epithelium) is a premalignant step in the H. pylori-driven progression toward gastric adenocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A hamartoma is a disorganized overgrowth of native tissue, not replacement of gastric epithelium by intestinal goblet and Paneth cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Goblet and Paneth cells are not normal in antral mucosa; they mark intestinal metaplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acute inflammation is neutrophilic and transient; intestinal metaplasia is a chronic adaptive change in cell type.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Viral cytopathic effect shows nuclear inclusions or multinucleation, not newly acquired goblet and Paneth cells.

questions.stem: In the H. pylori-driven gastric cascade, the left panel shows crowded, hyperchromatic nuclei (brackets) that then progress to the lesion in the right panel. What event marks this final transition?

explanation.summary: High-grade dysplasia becomes invasive gastric adenocarcinoma when the neoplastic cells invade through the basement membrane into surrounding tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: High-grade dysplasia becomes invasive gastric adenocarcinoma when the neoplastic cells invade through the basement membrane into surrounding tissues.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hyperplasia is a reversible increase in cell number without the nuclear atypia of dysplasia, and it is not the final step to carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gland loss characterizes atrophic gastritis, an earlier step in the cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acute neutrophilic inflammation marks active gastritis early in the sequence, not the transition to invasive cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Goblet cell formation defines intestinal metaplasia, which precedes dysplasia.

questions.stem: This gastric biopsy shows a dense proliferation of small, monotonous neoplastic B-lymphocytes in the mucosa of an H. pylori-infected patient. What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Extranodal marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma of the stomach is associated with H. pylori and shows an increased population of small neoplastic B-cells; many cases regress after eradication.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extranodal marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma of the stomach is associated with H. pylori and shows an increased population of small neoplastic B-cells; many cases regress after eradication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reactive follicular hyperplasia shows polarized germinal centers with mixed cells and tingible body macrophages, not monotonous neoplastic B cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by scattered Reed-Sternberg cells and almost never arises in the stomach.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gastric adenocarcinoma is an epithelial tumor forming glands or signet-ring cells, not sheets of small lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GIST is a spindle or epithelioid tumor of interstitial cells of Cajal that is KIT-positive and unrelated to H. pylori.

questions.stem: These axial contrast-enhanced chest CT images compare a normal mediastinum (left panel) with abnormal enlarged prevascular and paratracheal lymph nodes (right panel) in a young adult. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma classically presents with painless enlarged supradiaphragmatic (neck and mediastinal) lymphadenopathy, seen here as bulky anterior mediastinal and paratracheal adenopathy on CT.
explanation.whyCorrect: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma classically presents with painless enlarged supradiaphragmatic (neck and mediastinal) lymphadenopathy, seen here as bulky anterior mediastinal and paratracheal adenopathy on CT.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Small cell lung cancer usually affects older heavy smokers with a central lung mass and bulky nodes, not a young adult.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tuberculous lymphadenitis tends to produce necrotic, low-density nodes, usually right paratracheal or hilar, with lung findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sarcoidosis classically causes symmetric bilateral hilar adenopathy rather than bulky prevascular anterior mediastinal nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymoma is a single anterior mediastinal mass, typically in adults over 40, not multiple enlarged lymph nodes.

questions.stem: This endoscopic image shows an early, superficial mucosal lesion of the stomach detected on a screening program. Chronic infection with which organism is the major risk factor?

explanation.summary: Chronic H. pylori infection drives the stepwise cascade to gastric adenocarcinoma; endoscopic screening in high-incidence regions detects early, resectable lesions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic H. pylori infection drives the stepwise cascade to gastric adenocarcinoma; endoscopic screening in high-incidence regions detects early, resectable lesions.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HPV drives cervical, anal and oropharyngeal cancers, not gastric cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatitis B is a risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma, not gastric lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: EBV is linked to a small subset of gastric carcinomas, but chronic H. pylori is the major risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Schistosoma haematobium causes squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder, not gastric cancer.

questions.stem: This illustration depicts a child from an equatorial African region with a rapidly enlarging mass distorting the mandible. This presentation is classic for which neoplasm?

explanation.summary: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma is virtually always EBV-positive and classically presents in African children as a large, rapidly growing mandibular/jaw mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma is virtually always EBV-positive and classically presents in African children as a large, rapidly growing mandibular/jaw mass.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Osteosarcoma usually arises in the metaphysis of long bones in adolescents and is not tied to equatorial Africa or EBV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ewing sarcoma arises in the diaphysis of long bones or pelvis with an onion-skin periosteal reaction, not as an African jaw mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Langerhans cell histiocytosis causes lytic skull and bone lesions with Birbeck granules, without a geographic predilection for Africa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ameloblastoma is a slow-growing odontogenic tumor of adults, not a rapidly enlarging childhood mass.

questions.stem: This gross cross-section of liver shows a large hemorrhagic mass arising within a background of chronic liver injury. Chronic infection with which virus is the most common global cause of this tumor?

explanation.summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma most often arises from longstanding inflammation-mediated cellular damage and cirrhosis; hepatitis B virus is the leading worldwide cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatocellular carcinoma most often arises from longstanding inflammation-mediated cellular damage and cirrhosis; hepatitis B virus is the leading worldwide cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HTLV-1 causes adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not liver cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: EBV is linked to Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma, not hepatocellular carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma and primary effusion lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HPV causes cervical, anogenital and oropharyngeal squamous cancers, not liver tumors.

questions.stem: The left image shows a raised, rough papule on a child's finger and the right shows its histology with a hyperkeratotic squamous proliferation. Which HPV serotypes typically cause these benign lesions?

explanation.summary: Verruca vulgaris (common warts) are benign hyperkeratotic squamous papillomas caused by low-risk HPV serotypes 1, 2, 4, and 7.
explanation.whyCorrect: Verruca vulgaris (common warts) are benign hyperkeratotic squamous papillomas caused by low-risk HPV serotypes 1, 2, 4, and 7.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk types causing cervical dysplasia and carcinoma, not common warts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HPV 6 and 11 cause genital warts (condyloma acuminatum) and laryngeal papillomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HPV 5 and 8 are linked to epidermodysplasia verruciformis and skin cancer in immunosuppressed patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HPV 31 and 33 are high-risk anogenital types associated with cervical neoplasia.

questions.stem: This bladder biopsy shows parasitic eggs bearing a terminal spine surrounded by chronic inflammation. Long-term infection with this parasite predisposes to which malignancy?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small cell carcinoma of the bladder

explanation.summary: Schistosoma haematobium eggs (terminal spine) cause chronic bladder inflammation and metaplasia, predisposing to squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder.
explanation.whyCorrect: Schistosoma haematobium eggs (terminal spine) cause chronic bladder inflammation and metaplasia, predisposing to squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Renal cell carcinoma arises from tubular epithelium and is linked to smoking and VHL, not schistosomal bladder infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urothelial carcinoma is the most common bladder cancer overall, but chronic schistosomal irritation causes squamous metaplasia and then squamous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bladder adenocarcinoma is associated with urachal remnants and exstrophy rather than schistosomiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Small cell carcinoma of the bladder is rare and neuroendocrine, without a link to Schistosoma infection.

questions.stem: In this immunohistochemical panel for mismatch-repair proteins, the upper two markers show absent (loss of brown nuclear) staining in the tumor glands while the lower two retain intact brown staining. What does this pattern indicate about the tumor?

choices.label: E
choices.text: It has fully intact mismatch repair

explanation.summary: Loss of nuclear staining for MLH1 and PMS2 (which form a heterodimer, so loss of MLH1 destabilizes PMS2) with preserved MSH2/MSH6 indicates a mismatch-repair-deficient tumor. Such deficiency underlies microsatellite instability and is characteristic of Lynch-syndrome-associated cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of nuclear staining for MLH1 and PMS2 (which form a heterodimer, so loss of MLH1 destabilizes PMS2) with preserved MSH2/MSH6 indicates a mismatch-repair-deficient tumor. Such deficiency underlies microsatellite instability and is characteristic of Lynch-syndrome-associated cancers.

whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 mutations impair homologous recombination and are not detected by loss of MLH1 and PMS2 staining.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HER2 overexpression shows strong brown membrane staining on a HER2 stain, not loss of nuclear mismatch-repair proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Normal tissue retains nuclear staining for all four mismatch-repair proteins and acts as the internal positive control.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intact mismatch repair would show preserved nuclear staining for all four markers, not loss of the upper two.

questions.stem: This patient shows extreme photosensitivity with dense freckling and lesions concentrated on sun-exposed skin of the face and neck. An inherited defect in which DNA repair pathway underlies this presentation?

explanation.summary: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from loss-of-function mutations in nucleotide excision repair, leaving patients unable to remove UV-induced pyrimidine dimers, producing severe photosensitivity, freckling in sun-exposed areas, and greatly increased skin cancer risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from loss-of-function mutations in nucleotide excision repair, leaving patients unable to remove UV-induced pyrimidine dimers, producing severe photosensitivity, freckling in sun-exposed areas, and greatly increased skin cancer risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nonhomologous end joining repairs double-strand breaks; its defect causes ataxia telangiectasia-type features rather than UV photosensitivity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Homologous recombination defects (BRCA1/2) predispose to breast and ovarian cancer, not extreme sun sensitivity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Base excision repair fixes damaged single bases, such as oxidized or deaminated ones, and does not remove UV pyrimidine dimers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome with colon and endometrial cancer, not photosensitivity and freckling.

questions.stem: This schematic shows the MSH2-MSH6 complex identifying an error in newly synthesized DNA and the MLH1-PMS2 complex excising the incorrect base before resynthesis. Germline loss of the pathway shown predisposes to which hereditary cancer syndrome?

explanation.summary: The figure depicts mismatch repair. Germline mutation of a mismatch-repair gene (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) causes Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer), producing microsatellite instability and markedly increased colorectal and endometrial cancer risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: The figure depicts mismatch repair. Germline mutation of a mismatch-repair gene (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) causes Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer), producing microsatellite instability and markedly increased colorectal and endometrial cancer risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair of UV damage, not mismatch repair.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ataxia telangiectasia results from ATM mutation and impaired double-strand break signaling and repair.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Li-Fraumeni syndrome is caused by germline TP53 mutation, a cell cycle checkpoint gene rather than mismatch repair.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Familial adenomatous polyposis results from germline APC mutation in the WNT pathway, causing hundreds of polyps.

questions.stem: These images show dilated tortuous blood vessels in the conjunctiva of the eye (A) and on the skin (B, C) of the same patient, who developed ataxia, chorea, and neuropathy before age five. A defect in which DNA repair mechanism causes this disorder?

explanation.summary: The dilated vessels (telangiectasia) with early-onset ataxia indicate ataxia telangiectasia, caused by defective nonhomologous end joining of double-strand breaks. The same defect impairs V(D)J recombination, producing immunodeficiency, and predisposes to leukemia and lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The dilated vessels (telangiectasia) with early-onset ataxia indicate ataxia telangiectasia, caused by defective nonhomologous end joining of double-strand breaks. The same defect impairs V(D)J recombination, producing immunodeficiency, and predisposes to leukemia and lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Homologous recombination defects (BRCA1/2) predispose to breast and ovarian cancer without telangiectasia or childhood ataxia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nucleotide excision repair defects cause xeroderma pigmentosum, with photosensitivity and skin cancers rather than ataxia and telangiectasia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Base excision repair defects (e.g., MUTYH) cause colorectal polyposis, not neurologic disease with telangiectasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome with colorectal and endometrial cancer in adulthood.

questions.stem: This high-power H&E field shows sheets of small round-to-oval cells with scant cytoplasm, high nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed "salt-and-pepper" chromatin, and prominent nuclear molding. From which cell type does this tumor most characteristically arise?

explanation.summary: The morphology (small blue cells, scant cytoplasm, nuclear molding, dispersed chromatin) is that of small cell lung carcinoma, a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine tumor derived from Kulchitsky cells. This origin explains its capacity for ectopic hormone production (ACTH, ADH) and neurologic paraneoplastic syndromes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The morphology (small blue cells, scant cytoplasm, nuclear molding, dispersed chromatin) is that of small cell lung carcinoma, a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine tumor derived from Kulchitsky cells. This origin explains its capacity for ectopic hormone production (ACTH, ADH) and neurologic paraneoplastic syndromes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mesothelial cells give rise to mesothelioma, which is pleural-based with epithelioid or sarcomatoid cells, not small blue cells with molding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type II pneumocytes are linked to lepidic adenocarcinoma, which grows along alveolar walls with glandular cells and abundant cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucin-producing glandular epithelium gives rise to adenocarcinoma, which forms glands and lacks salt-and-pepper chromatin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinizing squamous epithelium gives rise to squamous cell carcinoma, with keratin pearls and intercellular bridges.

questions.stem: This abnormal cervical cytology (Pap smear) preparation shows a cluster of atypical cells adjacent to a normal squamous cell. The change demonstrated here is most directly caused by persistent infection with which agent?

explanation.summary: The enlarged, hyperchromatic cells with increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio represent a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). This precancerous dysplasia of the cervix is caused by persistent infection with high-risk strains of human papillomavirus (HPV), which is why HPV testing has become a key screening tool alongside the Pap smear.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enlarged, hyperchromatic cells with increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio represent a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). This precancerous dysplasia of the cervix is caused by persistent infection with high-risk strains of human papillomavirus (HPV), which is why HPV testing has become a key screening tool alongside the Pap smear.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia trachomatis causes cervicitis with inclusion-bearing cells but does not drive squamous dysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytomegalovirus produces large cells with owl-eye inclusions, not precancerous squamous lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV raises the risk of cervical neoplasia through immunosuppression, but the dysplasia itself is caused by HPV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Herpes simplex causes multinucleated cells with nuclear molding and margination, not high-grade dysplasia.

questions.stem: The clustered bright specks seen on this screening breast X-ray (left) prompted a biopsy showing the neoplastic changes at right. This finding is a suspicious marker for which early breast lesion?

explanation.summary: The mammogram shows clustered microcalcifications, a classic early sign of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Biopsy reveals neoplastic cells expanding a duct without invasion past the basement membrane, along with the characteristic chunky intraductal calcifications. Detecting DCIS by mammography allows treatment before progression to invasive disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mammogram shows clustered microcalcifications, a classic early sign of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Biopsy reveals neoplastic cells expanding a duct without invasion past the basement membrane, along with the characteristic chunky intraductal calcifications. Detecting DCIS by mammography allows treatment before progression to invasive disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibroadenoma is a benign, well-circumscribed mass and may develop coarse popcorn calcifications, not fine clustered microcalcifications.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paget disease of the breast presents with a crusted, eczematous nipple from intraepidermal tumor cells, not as clustered calcifications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Invasive lobular carcinoma rarely calcifies and grows in single-file lines of discohesive cells; it is invasive, not an early in situ lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phyllodes tumor is a large fibroepithelial mass with leaf-like stromal fronds, not clustered microcalcifications.

questions.stem: These lesions, including a pedunculated example and one with a velvety surface, are removed during colonoscopy. Left in place, they are the principal precursor to which malignancy?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

explanation.summary: The images show colonic adenomas (adenomatous polyps). Through the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, crowded neoplastic glands progressively accumulate mutations and can invade beyond the basement membrane into the lamina propria, giving rise to colorectal adenocarcinoma. Screening colonoscopy allows their removal before malignant transformation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The images show colonic adenomas (adenomatous polyps). Through the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, crowded neoplastic glands progressively accumulate mutations and can invade beyond the basement membrane into the lamina propria, giving rise to colorectal adenocarcinoma. Screening colonoscopy allows their removal before malignant transformation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GIST arises from interstitial cells of Cajal in the wall, mostly in the stomach, and is not preceded by mucosal adenomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anal squamous cell carcinoma is HPV-driven from squamous epithelium, not from colonic glandular polyps.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MALT lymphoma arises from lymphoid tissue, typically in the stomach with H. pylori, not from adenomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuroendocrine tumors arise from enteroendocrine cells deep in the mucosa, not through the adenoma-carcinoma sequence.
